I mostly posted in the smaller subreddits so the smaller Voat community seems like a welcome change of pace for me. One of the things that frustrated me about Reddit was that it was impossible to join in on the major conversations without being in on the ground floor or hijacking a top comment. I think that's a necessary evil with large communities though and I'm sure Voat also has places like that.

Generally I'm very optimistic about this place and looking forward to getting involved. Nice to meet all of you.

The article makes a good argument based on recent history. However, as an Albertan with an NDP government. I honestly feel that things are different this time around. However, this campaign has had a very different narrative. Trudeau had some very good press about a year ago, but now that his platform is revealed, he's looking a bit too right wing (well, from a leftist's perspective). In very simple terms of left and right, the Liberal Party seems to support some right wing platforms (such as C-51). Based on the anger vote, the NDP could be scooping up some votes from the LPC and CPC to form a minority government. However, I'm cautiously optimistic because it's still very early.
